description: Drone synthesiser: one of thirty-seven self-contained voices sounding at a time, played from a fundamental and a level, with a crossfade whenever the voice is changed

params.text: Sets the fundamental of the engine, five octaves either side of middle C
Chooses which of the thirty-seven engines is sounding; the display shows its name, and changing it fades the old one out and the new one in

inputs.text: Moves the fundamental, one volt per octave by default, or 100Hz per volt with the menu set to linear
Added to the amp knob, ten points of level per volt
Sweeps the engine selection across the whole bank, 0V for the first and 10V for the last

outputs.text: The left side of the engine, about ±5V with a soft limiter on the peaks
The right side of the engine, about ±5V with a soft limiter on the peaks

notes: this makes sound as soon as it is placed. There is no gate or trigger: the engine drones from the moment the module is in the rack.
several engines are genuinely stereo, so the two outputs differ; others give the same signal on both.
menu: Engine — the whole bank as a list, with the engine now sounding ticked
Engine bank — dræn (dronecaster ports) or hyf (original instruments); switching banks fades like an engine change
Hz CV input — 1V/oct, which tracks pitch, or Linear (100 Hz/V), which adds a flat number of hertz per volt
Fade time — how long each fade down and up takes on an engine change: 0.25 s, 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s or 8 s

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
